question: The outermost regions (ORs) face permanent constraints to their development, as recognised in Article 349 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. In particular, their remoteness from mainland Europe entails considerable extra costs, particularly transport costs, as the ORs depend on air and sea connections for passenger transport and the supply of goods.

A recent study by the Policy Department for Structural and Cohesion Policies on behalf of the REGI Committee (entitled ‘Cohesion Policy in the outermost regions’) recognises the need to improve the mobility of people and the accessibility of goods to reduce two major barriers to development.

In view of one of the recommendations made in the study to support sustainable transport development in the ORs, and in recognition of the importance of accessibility and mobility in these regions: 1.

Does the Commission intend to look into setting up a POSEI-like support scheme targeting the transport sector, so that these regions can play a part in the mandatory shift to more sustainable transport modes, as Parliament called for in its resolution (2022/2147(INI)) on the assessment of the new Commission communication on ORs?
What alternatives is it developing to meet these needs in these regions?
answer: The Commission recognises the dependence of outermost regions on transport for the supply of goods, people's mobility and for trade and tourism. These regions’ specificities are embedded in EU policies, legislative proposals and programmes, as envisaged in the 2022 revised strategy for the outermost regions (1).
The European Regional Development Fund (2) can, exclusively for these regions, finance airport infrastructure and compensate for their higher operating costs in transport.

The Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) (3) supports transport infrastructure with higher co-financing rates in these regions, and — once adopted — the revised Trans-European transport network Regulation (4) will increase the number of ports, airports, and urban nodes eligible for CEF funding.

The Commission has considered the connectivity needs of the outermost regions in the revised Emissions Trading System (ETS) (5). Domestic flights and maritime journeys between an outermost region and any other airport or port in the same Member State — including flights and sea voyages within the same outermost region — are exempted from the ETS until 2030. Around EUR 1.

6 billion has been set aside from the ETS revenues to cover the price difference between the use of eligible sustainable aviation fuels and of fossil kerosene until 2030. In outermost regions’ airports, these funds can exceptionally cover the full price difference resulting from the use of these fuels compared with fossil kerosene.

Communication ‘Putting people first, securing sustainable and inclusive growth, unlocking the potential of the EU’s outermost regions’, COM/2022/198 final. Proposals for new programmes, such as the one proposed by the Honourable member, will feed into discussions on the post2027 Multiannual Financial Framework. The Commission favours complementarities and synergies in making the most of all opportunities under EU funds.
